claim: First open-source LPEC decoder producing actual PCM audio from Sony .dvf/.msv files. The synthesis chain is wired on top of the F-51 bit-exact frame parser: per-frame LSF vector reconstruction from the LPEC.dll codebook stages (exact, decompile-derived), LSF-to-LPC conversion (public Chebyshev P/Q math incl. the (1+-z^-1) factors), per-frame 16-step (or 2x8-step for dual-LSP frames) linear LSF interpolation with a direct-form synthesis filter, and a best-effort excitation path (pitch-lag impulse/noise excitation with the per-band amplitude rows, codebook-page 4-segment cross-fade blend per the decompiled FUN_10004960 formula, single per-file peak normalization). Output is plausibility-validated (duration exactness, frame continuity, energy structure), NOT sample-validated against Sony reference output.
validation_basis: plausibility only - no Sony decoder output available for ground truth comparison

inputs.codec_tables: LPEC.dll (user-owned Digital Voice Editor 3.3.01) read at runtime via embedded PE VA->offset mapping; table addresses from F-48/F-52 decompilation; table VALUES are not committed

exact_from_decompile: LSF vector = sum of stage tables at state+0xb4/0xb8/0xbc/(+0xc0 for 4-group SP): FUN_100064b0
LSF domain: cycles/sample normalized (short path scale 65536.0 confirms 0..0.5 range)
LSF min-gap/monotonic repair exists (FUN_100096c0); gap constant approximated 0.001

frame LSF schedule: type0 block0 -> 16 linear steps prev->cur; type0 block1 -> 2x8 steps prev->avg->cur with avg=(prev+cur)/2 (const _DAT_1006b418=0.5); types 1/2/3 -> 16 steps (FUN_1000f1c0, FUN_10005040)
dual-LSP frames read two sets into +0x1d8/+0x260 slots (FUN_10005bf0 param 1/2, stride 0x88)
excitation page blending: 8-double page = 4-segment cross-fade weights, formula per FUN_10004960 (page[3-s] weights held path, page[4+s] weights current path, A84/A88 window tables runtime-filled)

pitch block semantics: 7-bit index -> 128-entry double table at state+0xcc used as per-subframe scale; 6-bit rows A/B -> per-band (8/10) amplitude rows at state+0xd0/+0xd4, band amp = rowB[idxB][k] + rowA[idxA][k], clamped >0 (FUN_10005d50)

gain field re-interpreted: 7/8-bit g is a pitch lag for an IIR comb post-filter (FUN_1000f430/FUN_1000e4a0, delay g, taps from FUN_1000e4a0 with shape table at state+0xc4 stride 0x18), 6-bit sh selects the comb shape; g=0 bypasses the comb
PCM16 output: round(+0.5) saturating at +-32767/-32768 (FUN_100059e0, consts read: 0.5/32767/-32768)
frame sizes: 512 samples @8k, 1024 @16k per decoder state (+4=bytes, +8=samples, +0xc/+0x10 sub-slices); three gain segments per frame [held, sub1, sub2]
approximated: excitation source signal: pitch-lag impulse train (lag = g, voiced) or band-limited noise (g=0) with per-band amplitude envelope, positions evenly spread per band - Sony generates pulse positions from the coarse int16 LSF path (FUN_10004b10/FUN_1000a110/FUN_1000c680) and pulse values from three 8-bit-code-indexed tables (state+0xe0/0xe4/0xe8 with row lengths at DAT_10046984); not mirrored in this pass
comb post-filter replaced by periodicity in the excitation itself (mathematically overlapping effect, not sample-equivalent)
A84/A88 runtime windows (FUN_1000fa90 fills DAT_1004a040/DAT_1004b040) approximated as linear half-frame cross-fade ramps
absolute gain chain (f0-table scale x band rows x pulse values) not fully calibrated; one per-file peak normalization (0.7 FS) applied instead
FUN_10009dd0 LSF->LPC replaced by public Chebyshev P/Q recursion (verified stable, decaying impulse response)

remaining_gaps: pulse position/value generation (FUN_10004450 band allocator mirror + FUN_100060e0 table walk + FUN_1000c680 position transform) - largest remaining quality gap
comb post-filter coefficient computation FUN_1000e4a0 (lag-dependent 3-tap from shape tables) not mirrored
pitch pulse shaper FUN_1000f4e0 (1024-entry ramp tables DAT_10042970/DAT_10044970) not mirrored
A84/A88 window computation FUN_1000fa90 not mirrored
excitation value/sign bitstream fields are parsed as opaque budget blocks (F-51); their intra-band split is only derived, not read
absolute output level mapping uncalibrated (per-file normalization substituted)
policy: No Sony binaries, no decompiled code, no extracted table values committed. Decoder reads the user-owned LPEC.dll at runtime; committed artifacts are derived addresses, formulas, and statistics only.
